World Tuberculosis Day 2026 Observed
Thursday, 09 April 2026
943 Hits
Sevagram, Wardha, March 2026: On the occasion of World Tuberculosis Day 2026, Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram, in collaboration with the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) team, Sevagram, and the Tuberculosis Association of India, conducted a series of impactful awareness and outreach activities aimed at promoting a TB-free India.
The observance began on 24th March 2026 with a role play (drama) presented by nursing students in the waiting area of the Medicine Department. The performance effectively conveyed messages on tuberculosis awareness, prevention, and the importance of timely treatment. On the same day, World TB Day was also observed in the TB Ward, where staff and patients participated actively. Dr. Ajay Lanjewar, Nodal Officer, NTEP, addressed the gathering and emphasized key aspects of TB awareness and control.
On 25th March 2026, academic activities were organized, including six clinical case-based presentations on tuberculosis by various departments, along with a presentation on adverse drug reactions by the Department of Pharmacology. The session concluded with the distribution of certificates and prizes to the top three presentations, followed by refreshments.
Community outreach formed a significant part of the initiative. Field activities were conducted in collaboration with the Department of Community Medicine across multiple locations:
At Dwarika Nagar Anganwadi Centre, Sindhi Meghe Village, Wardha (30th March 2026), an awareness session was organized for approximately 30 women. The program was attended by healthcare staff including CHO Mrs. Vaishali Asole, ANM Mrs. Maya Sonurkar, and MPW Mr. Anil Aghao. Special guests included Dr. Vikram Datta, Dr. Rahule (NQOCN, New Delhi), and Dr. Anuj Mundra (In-charge, UHTC, MGIMS). Sessions covered TB symptoms, treatment, nutrition, stigma, and government support schemes such as Nikshay Mitra.
At Hanuman Mandir, Karanji Kaji Village (27th March 2026), a community program was conducted with participation from 30–35 villagers. Sessions were led by Mr. Surendra Belurkar and Mr. Sandeep Sute, focusing on TB awareness, treatment adherence, nutrition, and community responsibility.
At Ganeshpur (24th March 2026), under Kasturba Rural Health Training Centre, Anji Mothi, a program was conducted for 35 villagers. The session included contributions from Dr. Sujata, Dr. Viraj, Mr. Atul Katarkar, and Mr. Jayprakash More, highlighting causes, symptoms, prevention, and the importance of completing treatment. ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers, and Gram Panchayat members actively participated.
At Grampanchayat Bhavan, Dhamangaon Wathoda Village (23rd March 2026), a large-scale awareness program saw participation from around 50 villagers. The event was attended by local dignitaries including Panchayat Samiti Member Mr. Praful Kuchewar and other community leaders. Sessions were conducted by Dr. Utkarsha Wankhede, Mrs. Vidya Shende, Mrs. Ranjana Wani, and Mr. Sandeep Sute, focusing on early diagnosis, nutrition, sputum testing, and stigma reduction.
All programs emphasized early detection, adherence to treatment, proper nutrition, and utilization of government health services. Community engagement through ASHA workers, Anganwadi staff, and local governance bodies played a crucial role in the success of these initiatives.
Through these multifaceted efforts, MGIMS Sevagram reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening awareness, reducing stigma, and contributing actively towards the national goal of eliminating tuberculosis.
